g.title: Package production (MOD-013)
Implementation sources
Skill archive production
CLI candidate composition
The explicit --output-dir branch of main calls build_adapter_archives for a selected version; --check uses a temporary candidate. The remaining default-sync behavior is a recorded conformance gap.

Supported target descriptors, expected_adapter_files, render_skill_for_adapter, resource copying, build_adapter_archives, and archive/hash helpers turn canonical skill sources into target archives. They package existing instructions; they do not synthesize instructions from REM.

prepare_candidate orchestrates archive generation/validation, write_archive_metadata, and npm pack in an isolated prepared checkout. These production operations contribute to MOD-013; release-intent admission, qualification, candidate sealing, and publication coordination remain MOD-015 responsibilities in the shared implementation file.
Declares the npm package name, existing dist/ payload, public README and license, one rigorloop executable, and yaml dependency. Its scripts contain no command-code compilation or generation step.
Source inputs
Candidate output layouts

With an explicit isolated --output-dir and selected --version, main calls build_adapter_archives. The shared helper validates canonical inventory, applies declared frontmatter transformations, copies selected resources, renders target entrypoints, and writes one ZIP per supported target. Candidate generation does not install or publish.
Source inputs
Candidate output layouts

prepare_candidate uses an isolated prepared checkout, builds and validates target ZIPs, calls write_archive_metadata to overlay archive facts and their trusted index in the candidate package, then invokes npm pack --json --ignore-scripts --pack-destination on packages/rigorloop. Packaging steps are mapped here; Release retains selection, qualification, sealing, and publication decisions.
Canonical authored skill directories and their assets, references, and scripts. This pass inspected directory names and the generator, not SKILL.md contents.
Canonical thin target entrypoint templates selected by the codex and claude descriptors.
Supported target inventory, inclusion/transform rules, deterministic ZIP layout, and requested-version handling used by the wrapper.

Relative to the explicitly selected candidate output directory; {release} is the supplied archive version. Members include the Codex support entrypoint and .agents/skills/{skill}/ instruction/resource trees. This is a declared source-derived layout, not an existing or qualified artifact.

Relative to the same candidate output directory; members include the Claude Code support entrypoint and .claude/skills/{skill}/ instruction/resource trees. This is a declared source-derived layout, not an existing or qualified artifact.
Canonical package.json, README.md, LICENSE, existing dist/ JavaScript runtime, and bundled metadata inputs selected by the package allowlist. The CLI source is packaged, not generated from REM.

Archive-production and hash definitions used by the candidate coordinator. At execution, the coordinator also consumes the actual target ZIP bytes produced by Skill archive production; candidate ZIPs are outputs, not canonical repository inputs.
The candidate coordinator runs this archive validator successfully before calling write_archive_metadata; source inspection does not assert that validation ran for this architecture pass.

Relative to the selected candidate output directory; the filename is supplied by npm pack for @xiongxianfei/rigorloop. Its package/ tree contains the selected existing runtime and candidate dist/metadata overlay, with rigorloop mapped to dist/bin/rigorloop.js. No artifact was produced in this pass.

Relative to the candidate output directory; write_archive_metadata also copies the same metadata bytes into dist/metadata/ within the isolated package tree and updates that tree's releases.json trust index before packing.

Relative to the candidate output directory; write_archive_metadata records the source commit, archive identities, and archive-validation result for the preceding validated candidate sequence. The helper is not independent verification or public-release evidence; this pass does not execute or approve it.
